name: Maldives
genZNote: Maldives is Earth's sea-level canary — its highest natural point is barely taller than a speed bump, and a past president once held a full cabinet meeting underwater in scuba gear just to make that point on camera.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: An archipelago of roughly 1,192 coral islands grouped into 26 natural atolls in the Indian Ocean, southwest of India and Sri Lanka.
The lowest-lying country on Earth, with an average ground elevation of about 1.5 metres above sea level — making it exceptionally vulnerable to rising sea levels.
Only about 200 of its islands are inhabited; many others are dedicated resort islands or uninhabited.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Dhivehi is the national language, written in the distinctive Thaana script.
Sunni Islam is the state religion, and Maldivian law requires citizenship to be linked to being Muslim.
Culture blends South Asian, Arab, and East African influences, shaped by the islands' long history as an Indian Ocean trading crossroads.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic since 1968, when the centuries-old sultanate was abolished following a referendum.
Unicameral legislature: the People's Majlis.
Administratively divided into atolls, each with its own local council.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A global focal point for climate-change and sea-level-rise science, given its extreme low-lying geography.
Notable for coral reef research and marine conservation, given the ecological importance of its reef systems to both biodiversity and coastal protection.
Investing in land reclamation and elevated infrastructure (such as the artificial island of Hulhumalé) as adaptation measures to rising seas.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations, SAARC, and the Commonwealth of Nations (rejoined in 2020 after a period outside it).
A leading international voice on climate change and small-island-state vulnerability, including at UN climate conferences.
Maintains close ties with regional and Gulf partners for trade, tourism investment, and infrastructure financing.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India has historically been a first responder to the Maldives in crises — notably Operation Cactus (1988), when Indian forces helped repel an attempted coup.
India's 'Neighbourhood First' policy and SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) vision place the Maldives as a key Indian Ocean partner for maritime security and development assistance.
Operation Neer (2014) saw India rush emergency drinking water to Malé during a water crisis.
The relationship has seen periods of political strain (including a 2023-24 'India Out' domestic political campaign in the Maldives), alongside continuing economic and development cooperation.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Tourism, centred on luxury overwater resorts, is by far the largest sector and main source of government revenue and foreign exchange.
Fishing, especially tuna, is the second major traditional economic activity.
As a small island nation, the Maldives imports the large majority of its food, fuel, and construction materials.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Luxury overwater bungalow resorts and world-class diving and snorkelling on coral reefs.
Being the world's lowest-lying country, and a leading global voice on climate-change vulnerability and adaptation.
A largely tourism-dependent economy built on a chain of coral atolls.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR).
Tourism, centred on luxury island resorts, is the dominant economic sector, alongside fishing.
Among the smallest economies in Asia by population, but with high per-capita tourism revenue.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: The world's lowest-lying country, made up of coral atolls, with an average elevation of about 1.5 metres above sea level.
Extremely vulnerable to sea-level rise; a global advocate for climate action and marine conservation.
Home to extensive coral reef ecosystems supporting rich marine biodiversity.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: A historic Indian Ocean trading hub; converted to Islam in the 12th century.
Became independent from British protection in 1965; became a republic in 1968.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1965 independence from Britain; 1968 abolished the monarchy to become a republic.
The 2008 Constitution introduced multi-party democratic elections after decades of single-party rule.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Traditional Bodu Beru drumming and dance reflect its Indian Ocean cultural heritage.
A globally recognised luxury eco-tourism destination.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN and SAARC.
A prominent voice in international climate-change forums due to its existential vulnerability to sea-level rise.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Maldives is a low-lying Indian Ocean archipelago of coral atolls, a presidential republic since 1968, and the world's lowest-lying country by elevation.
keyFacts: Capital: Malé. Currency: Maldivian Rufiyaa. Language: Dhivehi.
About 1,192 coral islands across 26 atolls; average elevation ~1.5 m.
Became a republic in 1968, ending the historic sultanate.
Tourism is the dominant economic sector.
commonConfusion: The Maldives is a REPUBLIC (since 1968), not a monarchy — it is sometimes mixed up with Gulf monarchies due to shared Islamic identity.

highYieldFacts: World's lowest-lying country; average elevation ~1.5 metres — a frequently tested climate-vulnerability fact.
Became a republic in 1968; capital Malé; official language Dhivehi.
India's Operation Cactus (1988) and Operation Neer (2014) are key India-Maldives assistance episodes.
commonTraps: Confusing the Maldives with other Indian Ocean island nations (e.g. Seychelles, Mauritius) — the Maldives is specifically the lowest-lying and closest to India/Sri Lanka.
mustRemember: Maldives: 1,192-island coral atoll republic, lowest country on Earth, tourism-driven economy, close but sometimes strained relationship with India.
